Reference Translation (provided): In all parts He governs and them He reigns: there in His city and His lofty seat. O happy he whom thereto He elects!”

**Interpretation Lock – ONE BULLET PER SOURCE LINE**
- **Line 127** *In tutte parti impera e quivi regge;* → In every part of the world the Sovereign (He) **governs** those parts, and **there** (at the same place) He **reigns**. - **Line 128** *quivi è la sua città e l’alto seggio:* → At that very place there **is** the Sovereign’s **city** and His **lofty seat**. - **Line 129** *oh felice colui cu’ ivi elegge!* → “O happy” is the one **whom** He **elects** **there** (i.e., the one chosen for that place).

(eleg‑) | **elects** | He selects the individual at “there” | predicate verb |
*Notes*
- The Italian **quivi** and **ivi** both render English “there”, but in the source they serve distinct discourse functions: **quivi** points to the place of rule/reign, while **ivi** points to the place of election. - The contraction **l’** is the elided masculine definite article preceding the adjective **alto**; together they translate to “the lofty”. - Punctuation marks (semicolon, colon, exclamation) are not listed as lexical items but signal clause boundaries that correspond to the English punctuation in the reference.
